To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the change in insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) in diabetic patients with peripheral neuropathy was significantly correlated with the change in nerve conduction velocity (NCV), and 2) the change in IGF-1 in diabetic subjects with neuropathy was significantly related to the change in the amplitude of compound muscle action potentials.
the insulin-like growth factor (IGF)-I is decreased in diabetic patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) compared to diabetic patients without DPN.
IGF-1 is a potent neurotrophic factor that is reduced in the diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) patient and that the IGF-1 receptor (IGF-1R) is a key receptor in DPN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of diabetes on the IGF system in patients with neuropathy, with particular reference to the role of IGF-1 and IGFBP-1.
the role of IGF-I and IGF-II in the pathogenesis of diabetic neuropathy.
the effect of IGF-1 and its receptors on diabetic neuropathy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IGF-I level is significantly decreased in the diabetic neuropathy group, and the level of IGFBP-3 is increased in the diabetic neuropatic group.
the IGF-I system has a significant role in the pathogenesis of diabetic neuropathy.

the IGF-1 level in diabetic patients with peripheral neuropathy is significantly lower than that in diabetic patients without peripheral neuropathy, which indicates that IGF-1 may play a role in the pathogenesis of diabetic peripheral neuropathy, and the level of IGF-1 is negatively correlated with the severity of diabetic peripheral neuropathic symptoms, which may be a potential biomarker for predicting the severity of diabetic neuropathy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IGF-1 level is decreased in diabetic neuropathy and the IGF- 1 level may be a useful marker for diabetic neuropathy.
the change of insulin-like development factor-1 (IGF-1) in diabetic patients with peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is related to the severity of DPN.
the change of IGF-1 in diabetic neuropathy is related to the degree of nerve injury and is associated with the severity of diabetic peripheral neuropathy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IGF1 is a promising biomarker to detect the development of neuropathy in diabetic patients.
IGF-1 levels are lower in patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) compared to patients with diabetic retinopathy (DR) and healthy controls.
the IGF-1 receptor is a potential target for the treatment of diabetic neuropathy.
